# michi — Agent Instructions

## Commands

- Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`.
- `just test` — run all tests (Rust + Node)
- `just test-rust` — Rust tests only (cargo nextest)
- `just check` — fmt + clippy (`--all-targets`, single workspace-wide invocation, matches CI) + deny + typos + markdown fmt
- `just pre-push` — fmt-check + `lint-affected` (moon-detected affected crates only, one multi `-p` clippy invocation — not the full workspace)
- `just build-node` — compile NAPI binary for local platform
- `just bench` — run divan benchmarks
- `just snapshots` — review insta snapshot diffs
- `just coverage` — generate lcov.info

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code (tests OK with message)
- No `unsafe` outside napi boundary
- `BTreeMap` for output maps, `HashMap` for internal state only
- Pre-allocate strings with `String::with_capacity`
- Truncation uses char boundaries (`floor_char_boundary`)
- Every `pub` item has a doc comment
- NAPI: `version = "3"`, `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` on every export
- Benchmarks: divan (not criterion)
- Tests: `cargo nextest run` (not `cargo test`)

## Writing

- Write docs in plain, concise language. Keep them friendly and scannable; remove filler and AI-sounding prose.
- Comments should explain non-obvious choices, stay useful, and wrap at 120 columns.

## Philosophy

- Before adding a new primitive or judging whether work is "done," read `PRINCIPLES.md` — the inclusion checklist and process conventions this project runs on.

## Architecture

- `src/` — pure sync rendering library (default features: zero runtime deps)
- `crates/michi-pipeline/` — async pipeline execution (Plan 2, shipped): `execute_pipeline`/`execute_pipeline_parallel`, `CircuitBreaker`, `CancellationToken`, its own `ExecutionError` (not a `michi_core::Error` variant — see `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`). Depends on `michi-core` + `michi-resilience` + `tokio`; not re-exported through the root `michi` facade, versioned independently.
- `packages/michi-node/` — thin NAPI cdylib shim, npm package name `@orin-axi/michi`
- Feature flags: `napi`, `serde` (opt-in Serialize/Deserialize + `toon::list()`), `schemars`, `miette`. Plan 2 execution lands as separate crates when built, never as features here — `pipeline` has shipped this way (see `crates/michi-pipeline/` above); `fuzzy`/`cache`/`cli` remain unbuilt. See `docs/spec/01-overview-and-setup.md`'s Cargo.toml section for the current split.
- See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` for decisions
- See `docs/spec/` for full module API reference

## Module guide

| Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `toon` | TOON list rendering — token-optimized agent list format |
| `kv` | Key-value single-item rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` hint blocks |
| `truncate` | Token-safe content truncation |
| `empty` | Definitive empty state responses |
| `error` | Unified `michi::Error` type with agent rendering |
| `idempotency` | Partial-success reporting (`PartialSuccess`/`FailedOp`) — despite the name, idempotency keys and already-done detection live in `resilience` (`AlreadyDone`/`already_done()`), not here |
| `resilience` | Retry config, delay calculation, retry-after parsing |
| `status` | Health/status response rendering |
| `recovery` | Recovery hint blocks |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — composes all primitives |
| `mcp` | MCP `CallToolResult` assembly — always compiled, no feature gate |
| `audience` | `Audience` (assistant/user) — shared by `mcp` and `response::render_for()` |
| `pipeline` | Pipeline pure data type + render (execution now in `crates/michi-pipeline`, not this table's `src/`) |
| `telemetry` | No-op telemetry provider (`NoopProvider`) — zero-cost default, always compiled |

# michi — Agent Instructions

## Commands

- Always prefix shell commands with `rtk`.
- `just test` — run all tests (Rust + Node)
- `just test-rust` — Rust tests only (cargo nextest)
- `just check` — fmt + clippy (`--all-targets`, single workspace-wide invocation, matches CI) + deny + typos + markdown fmt
- `just pre-push` — fmt-check + `lint-affected` (moon-detected affected crates only, one multi `-p` clippy invocation — not the full workspace)
- `just build-node` — compile NAPI binary for local platform
- `just bench` — run divan benchmarks
- `just snapshots` — review insta snapshot diffs
- `just coverage` — generate lcov.info

## Non-negotiables

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code (tests OK with message)
- No `unsafe` outside napi boundary
- `BTreeMap` for output maps, `HashMap` for internal state only
- Pre-allocate strings with `String::with_capacity`
- Truncation uses char boundaries (`floor_char_boundary`)
- Every `pub` item has a doc comment
- NAPI: `version = "3"`, `#[napi(catch_unwind)]` on every export
- Benchmarks: divan (not criterion)
- Tests: `cargo nextest run` (not `cargo test`)

## Writing

- Write docs in plain, concise language. Keep them friendly and scannable; remove filler and AI-sounding prose.
- Comments should explain non-obvious choices, stay useful, and wrap at 120 columns.

## Philosophy

- Before adding a new primitive or judging whether work is "done," read `PRINCIPLES.md` — the inclusion checklist and process conventions this project runs on.

## Architecture

- Virtual Cargo workspace: the root `Cargo.toml` has no `[package]` and no shared version; Callisto writes each crate's `version` and keeps them equal (fixed group `michi`, lockstep releases, checked by CI version-sync)
- `crates/michi-core/` — pure sync rendering library, every primitive (default features: only `thiserror` + `compact_str`). Integration tests, divan benches and examples live in `crates/michi-core/{tests,benches,examples}` (`cargo run -p michi-core --example basic_toon`)
- `crates/michi-pipeline/` — async pipeline execution (Plan 2, shipped): validated `Plan` of `ExecStep`s, `execute`/`resume` returning a `RunRecord`, keyed `BreakerRegistry`, retry budget, `CancellationToken` (wraps tokio-util), `StepObserver`, its own `ExecutionError` (not a `michi_core::Error` variant — see `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`). API: `docs/spec/08-pipeline-execution.md`. Depends on `michi-core` (exact `=` version pin) + `tokio` + `tokio-util`; not re-exported through `michi-core`.
- `packages/michi-node/` — thin NAPI cdylib shim (`publish = false`), npm package name `@orin-dx/michi`; the exports themselves live in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` behind michi-core's `napi` feature and are re-exported via `pub use michi_core::napi::*;`
- Published crates: `michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` only. There is no `michi` crate (the name on crates.io belongs to an unrelated project)
- Feature flags (on `michi-core`): `napi`, `serde` (opt-in Serialize/Deserialize + `toon::list()`), `schemars`, `miette`. Plan 2 execution lands as separate crates when built, never as features here — `pipeline` has shipped this way (see `crates/michi-pipeline/` above); `fuzzy`/`cache`/`cli` remain unbuilt. See `docs/spec/01-overview-and-setup.md`'s Cargo.toml section for the current split.
- See `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-03-michi-design.md` for decisions
- See `docs/spec/` for full module API reference

## Module guide

All modules live in `crates/michi-core/src/`.

| Module | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `toon` | TOON list rendering — token-optimized agent list format |
| `kv` | Key-value single-item rendering |
| `hints` | `help[]` hint blocks |
| `truncate` | Token-safe content truncation |
| `empty` | Definitive empty state responses |
| `error` | Unified `michi_core::Error` type with agent rendering |
| `idempotency` | Partial-success reporting (`PartialSuccess`/`FailedOp`) — despite the name, idempotency keys and already-done detection live in `resilience` (`AlreadyDone`/`already_done()`), not here |
| `resilience` | Retry config, delay calculation, retry-after parsing |
| `status` | Health/status response rendering |
| `recovery` | Recovery hint blocks |
| `response` | `AgentResponse` builder — composes all primitives |
| `mcp` | MCP `CallToolResult` assembly — always compiled, no feature gate |
| `audience` | `Audience` (assistant/user) — shared by `mcp` and `response::render_for()` |
| `pipeline` | Pipeline pure data type + render (execution lives in `crates/michi-pipeline`, not `crates/michi-core`) |
| `telemetry` | No-op telemetry provider (`NoopProvider`) — zero-cost default, always compiled |
| `napi` | NAPI export surface for `@orin-dx/michi` (`napi` feature only) — the one module allowed `unsafe` |

</INSTRUCTIONS>

# Dependency graphs (`michi-graph`)

`michi-graph` validates and orders dependency graphs: steps in a pipeline, operations in a release, packages in a workspace, tasks in an agent's plan. It is MIT-licensed, has no dependencies (it is `no_std` with `alloc`), and depends on nothing else in michi, so permissive crates such as `callisto-model` can use it. `michi-pipeline` builds its `Plan` on it.

It is a small, deterministic graph model, not a general graph library. There are no node or edge payloads, no mutation after a graph is built, no path finding and no execution policy. The reasons for each choice are in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md), "michi-graph: an MIT leaf crate, versioned on its own".

## Vocabulary

- A **node** has a key `K: Ord + Clone` chosen by the caller (`StepId`, `PackageId`, `String`).
- An **edge** says that a **dependent** depends on a **prerequisite**: the prerequisite comes first. The API never says "from/to" or "in/out", because those words mean opposite things in different tools.
- Every edge has a **kind** `E: Ord`, which defaults to `()`. Callisto uses kinds such as runtime, dev and peer; michi and wisp don't use kinds.
- A `NodeIx` is a node's declaration position: the first node declared is 0. It has no public constructor. Every method that takes one returns an empty slice or `None` for an index the graph does not have, so an index from another graph never panics.

## Building

```rust
let mut b = GraphBuilder::<StepId>::with_capacity(steps.len());
for step in &steps {
    let node = b.node(step.id().clone());
    for prerequisite in step.prerequisites() {
        b.depends_on(node, prerequisite, ());
    }
}
let graph = b.build(UnknownTargets::Error);
```

- `node(key)` declares a node and returns a `Decl` token. Edges hang off the token, not the key. A later node reusing a key is recorded as a duplicate, and its edges are dropped with it, so they can never land on the first node and cause false errors.
- `depends_on(decl, prerequisite, kind)` takes the prerequisite key, which may be declared before or after. An edge repeated with the same kind collapses into one.
- `build(policy)` never fails. It sets aside what it cannot use and records why, so every problem can be reported later in one list:
  - a duplicate node;
  - an edge to a key no node has (a **dangling** edge). It is always kept in `Graph::dangling()`. The `UnknownTargets` policy only decides whether validation reports it: `Error` reports it as `UnknownDependency`, and `Ignore` doesn't (Callisto ignores dependencies on packages outside the workspace);
  - more than `u32::MAX` nodes.
- A node that depends on itself is kept as an ordinary edge, and the edge filter decides whether it counts (a dev-only self-dependency is legal in Cargo).
- `Dag::from_nodes(iter, order)` builds and validates in one call for the common case: no kinds and unknown targets are errors.

## Graph and Dag

A `Graph<K, E>` may contain cycles. A `Dag<K>` is proven acyclic and carries no kinds, because validation has already chosen which edges count.

- `graph.validate(order)` uses every edge; `graph.validate_filtered(keep, order)` keeps only the edges for which `keep(EdgeRef)` returns true. `EdgeRef` has named fields: `dependent`, `prerequisite`, `kind` and both `NodeIx`s. Keys are shared between the graph and its dags, so validating does not copy them.
- One graph can produce several dags. Callisto validates its package graph once without dev edges for cascade order, and once with them for publish order.
- Validation returns the `Dag` or a `Violations` list with every problem at once. Cycles made only of filtered-out edges are not problems: you validate the graph you will run.
- When several kinds connect the same pair and more than one passes the filter, the dag holds one edge. `prerequisites` and `dependents` never repeat a node.
- `graph.cycles(keep, order)` reports the cycles of a graph that is allowed to have them (lumen's agent trajectories).

## Order

The caller chooses how ties are broken, once, at validation:

- `Order::Declaration`: the earliest-declared node first. Steps run in the order they were written. michi uses this.
- `Order::Key`: the smallest key first. Shuffling the declarations changes nothing. Callisto uses this, because it seals its release plan with a digest.

Everything the crate outputs follows that one order: the topological order, each layer, `ready`, `ancestors`, `descendants`, cycle members and the order of the violations' cycles. The topological order is the lexicographically smallest valid order under that rule, and that is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. The order never comes from hash maps or traversal accidents.

## Queries on a Dag

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `order()` | `&[NodeIx]` in topological order, computed at validation |
| `keys_in_order()` | the keys in that order |
| `prerequisites(ix)`, `dependents(ix)` | `&[NodeIx]` neighbours, in the chosen order |
| `layers()` | layer 0 has no prerequisites; a node's layer is one more than its deepest prerequisite's. Nodes in one layer don't depend on each other, so they can run together |
| `ready(satisfied, eligible)` | nodes for which `eligible(key)` holds and `satisfied(p)` holds for every prerequisite, in order |
| `ancestors(roots)`, `descendants(roots)` | every node upstream or downstream of `roots`, not including them |
| `key(ix)`, `index_of(&key)`, `node_at(position)`, `len()` | lookups; `node_at` maps a declaration position to its node, for callers that keep per-node data in declaration order |
| `canonical()` | each node's key with its prerequisites' keys, nodes and prerequisites sorted by key, for callers that hash the structure with their own hasher. Isolated nodes are included |

`ready` takes two predicates because callers track more than "done". A node behind a failure must not become ready, and a running or failed node is not eligible to start. When `satisfied` holds only for nodes that succeeded, checking direct prerequisites is enough: a node whose prerequisite failed can never become ready.

`ready` is one pass over the graph, O(V + E). There is no incremental ready tracker: michi's scheduler keeps its own counters because what unblocks a step depends on the outcome, and Callisto's release plans are small. A tracker can be added later without a breaking change if a consumer measures a need.

## Violations

`Violation<K>` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and holds keys, cloned only on the error path:

- `DuplicateNode { key }`
- `UnknownDependency { dependent, prerequisite }`
- `SelfDependency { key }`: reported once per node, never as a cycle.
- `Cycle(Cycle<K>)`: `members()` lists every node of one strongly connected component, in the chosen order. `path()` is one shortest closed path through the first member, so a message can show a real loop.
- `TooManyNodes`

`Violations<K>` lists them in a fixed order: duplicates, then edge problems by the dependent's declaration position and the edge's position, then cycles in the chosen order. The same input always gives the same list.

`Display` exists when `K: Display`, and `display_with(|key, f| ...)` covers keys without it. A cycle reads as `a depends on b, which depends on c, which depends on a`. The printed path stops after 8 steps with `… and N more`; the struct keeps the whole path. `Violations<K>` implements `core::error::Error` when `K: Debug + Display`.

## Implementation rules

- No recursion: Kahn's algorithm for the order and an iterative Kosaraju for strongly connected components. A 100,000-node chain and a 100,000-node cycle are tested.
- Kahn's leftovers are always an error: nodes on or behind a cycle never disappear silently. Strongly connected components are computed only on those leftovers, so a valid graph doesn't pay for them.
- Adjacency is `u32` indices in sorted vectors; keys live once in an `Arc<[K]>`, and a key-sorted index permutation answers `index_of` by binary search.
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, unchecked indexing or `unsafe` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`).

## How michi-pipeline uses it

- `Plan::new` declares one node per step, builds with `UnknownTargets::Error` and validates with `Order::Declaration`. Violations map one to one onto `PlanViolation`. Cycles stay a single `PlanViolation::Cycle` listing every step on any cycle in declaration order, and `TooManyNodes` becomes `PlanViolation::TooManySteps`. One change: a step stuck between two cycles (depending on one, depended on by another) lies on no cycle and is no longer listed.
- The scheduler reads `order()`, `prerequisites` and `dependents`. Node indices are declaration positions, so they match `Plan::steps()` and `RunRecord` without translation. Its ready counters, failure skipping and resume seeding stay in michi-pipeline: they are execution policy.
- `PlanFingerprint` stays michi's own 64-bit FNV-1a with its current framing, computed over `canonical()`. A record saved before the change still resumes.
- No michi-graph type appears in michi-pipeline's public API, so a michi-graph release never forces a breaking michi-pipeline release. michi-pipeline depends on it with a normal `^` range, not the exact pin the lockstep crates use.

## Licensing and release

- `license = "MIT"` in the crate's own manifest and a crate `LICENSE`; the rest of the workspace stays FSL-1.1-MIT.
- CI walks the normal and build dependencies of `michi-graph` with `cargo metadata` and fails on any license outside the permissive allowlist, so no FSL crate can enter its tree.
- It versions on its own, outside the Callisto fixed group `michi`. A michi-graph minor release moves michi-pipeline out of its `^` range, so Callisto's cascade also bumps the michi group.

# Principles

Two questions come up over and over: **should this go in michi?** and **how should this work get done?** This doc answers both, so nobody — human or agent — has to re-derive the reasoning from scratch each time. It's the "why" behind `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s rules, not a replacement for either.

---

## What belongs in michi

A primitive earns a place here only if it clears all five gates below. These are yes/no checks with evidence, not vibes — if you can't point to the evidence, it doesn't clear the gate yet.

### 1. Rendering, not domain logic

It turns already-decided data into agent-readable strings/types. It doesn't decide _what_ data survives.

- One established exception: char/byte-level truncation (`truncate`, `ToonOptions::max_cell_len`) — treated as rendering safety, not business logic.
- **The ceiling:** if a tool's real need is more sophisticated than a generic primitive can serve — a custom ranking algorithm, a heuristic tuned to one tool's data shape — that's a sign the primitive doesn't belong in michi, not a sign to make michi's primitive more complex. See [Split the decision from the signal](#split-the-decision-from-the-signal) for how to resolve this without compromising on either.

### 2. Small default dependency set

The default build depends only on `thiserror` and `compact_str`. Anything else is opt-in behind a Cargo feature.

- Adding a mandatory dependency needs a recorded decision in `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`. Prefer caller-supplied injection (a closure, a trait) first.

### 3. Genuinely cross-tool — verified, not assumed

Earns inclusion when independent, real tools would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern.

- "Independent" and "real" are load-bearing. One tool using a pattern heavily is one data point, not proof.
- **What clearing this bar looks like:** a survey across several real agent-facing dev tools (a code-search engine, a CLI proxy, a context-compression tool, a code-graph server) found `help[]`-shaped "note for the agent" hints independently reinvented, inconsistently, in every one of them.
- A pattern seen in only one tool — however heavily repeated inside that tool — isn't there yet. Watch for a second independent confirmation before building it.

### 4. Doesn't duplicate an existing primitive

Check `hints` / `recovery` / `idempotency` / `status` / `error` / `mcp` first. Verify the distinction concretely — don't assume novelty from a vibe.

- "This looks similar to X" means go read X's source, not assume it's covered.
- Example: a proposed "diagnostics" primitive looked adjacent to `idempotency::PartialSuccess` — until actually reading `PartialSuccess`'s doc comment showed it's scoped to multi-step _mutating_ operations, not read-path degradation. They turned out genuinely distinct, but that took checking, not assuming either way.

### 5. Deviations get tracked, not silently absorbed

Where the final shape diverges from the original ask or an earlier draft, it goes in a Design Decisions table. Spec and code should never quietly drift apart.

---

## Split the decision from the signal

Gate 1's ceiling ("stay generic" vs. "real tools need real sophistication") isn't a tension to compromise on — it's usually an architecture problem. Separate the _domain-specific decision_ from the _universal signal_.

**Worked example: truncation.** Deciding _which_ items survive a budget is tool-specific — personalized-PageRank over a call graph, a statistical outlier-preserving sampler, a simple first-N cutoff. None of that belongs in michi. But _reporting_ what got cut, in a consistent agent-readable shape, is exactly what every tool needs regardless of how it decided.

That split shipped as `michi_core::truncation` (API in [`docs/spec/03-rust-api.md`](docs/spec/03-rust-api.md#truncation--what-a-list-cap-cut)): `TruncationOutcome<T>` holds what was kept and the total before the cut, `hint(guidance)` gives the standard `help[]` line, `truncate_by_count` and `truncate_by_size` are the two strategies michi ships, and `AgentResponse::truncation` sets the count and the hint together. Where the shipped shape differs from the first sketch (a derived `truncated()` instead of a stored flag, a public `new()`, `truncate_by_size` instead of `truncate_by_bytes`), the reasons are in [`docs/spec/06-decisions.md`](docs/spec/06-decisions.md).

A caller with a genuinely novel heuristic never has to fit their algorithm into michi's shape — they wrap whatever they decided with `TruncationOutcome::new` and get the same hint/report format everyone else gets. Michi owns the contract, not the heuristic.

**When a new primitive seems too domain-specific to generalize, ask whether it splits this way first.** Often only half of it actually is.

---

## How work gets done

Heuristics, not hard rules — process needs contextual judgment the content checklist doesn't.

### 1. TDD, always

Failing test first, verified red for the right reason, then implementation, then green. No implementation code without a preceding red test.

### 2. Independent verification before "done"

A separate pass re-checks against the spec by running the actual output — not by trusting the implementer's self-report or re-reading the diff.

- Per-task review alone has missed real bugs that a separately-scoped validation pass, checking actual wire output, caught.
- "Every task's reviewer said pass" and "the feature actually works" are different questions. Both need answering.

### 3. Verify before asserting

Claims about external state — a registry's current contents, another project's actual spec, a dependency's real behavior — get checked directly, not recalled from memory or assumed from a plausible-sounding claim.

- Can't quickly re-verify something? Say so rather than asserting confidence.

### 4. History is append-only

Superseded plans/specs get a notice pointing at what replaced them, not a rewrite pretending they always said the current thing.

- A plan document that was correct when written stays as written. Corrections happen in new commits, not retroactive edits to old ones.

### 5. Publish/release gates are earned

Passing a component's own tests isn't "ready to ship."

- Release checks should cover package contents, compatibility promises, security, and the intended release scope. Consumer integration can be a post-release check when a published package is needed to perform that integration.

### 6. Invariant enforcement policy

Three patterns apply at different layers. Pick the right one for the layer — don't invent a fourth.

- **Infallible constructors normalize.** `new()` clamps inputs to valid ranges silently (e.g. `jitter_factor` to `[0.0, 1.0]`, `base_delay` to `≤ max_delay`). Never `unwrap()`/`expect()` in lib code. Expose a `try_new()` or `validate()` alongside for callers who want explicit error signals — but these are additive, they don't replace the normalizing constructor.

# Principles

Two questions come up over and over: **should this go in michi?** and **how should this work get done?** This doc answers both, so nobody — human or agent — has to re-derive the reasoning from scratch each time. It's the "why" behind `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CLAUDE.md`'s rules, not a replacement for either.

---

## What belongs in michi

A primitive earns a place here only if it clears all five gates below. These are yes/no checks with evidence, not vibes — if you can't point to the evidence, it doesn't clear the gate yet.

### 1. Rendering, not domain logic

It turns already-decided data into agent-readable strings/types. It doesn't decide _what_ data survives.

- One established exception: char/byte-level truncation (`truncate`, `ToonOptions::max_cell_len`) — treated as rendering safety, not business logic.
- **The ceiling:** if a tool's real need is more sophisticated than a generic primitive can serve — a custom ranking algorithm, a heuristic tuned to one tool's data shape — that's a sign the primitive doesn't belong in michi, not a sign to make michi's primitive more complex. See [Split the decision from the signal](#split-the-decision-from-the-signal) for how to resolve this without compromising on either.

### 2. Small default dependency set

The default build depends only on `thiserror` and `compact_str`. Anything else is opt-in behind a Cargo feature.

- Adding a mandatory dependency needs a recorded decision in `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`. Prefer caller-supplied injection (a closure, a trait) first.

### 3. Genuinely cross-tool — verified, not assumed

Earns inclusion when independent, real tools would otherwise hand-roll the identical pattern.

- "Independent" and "real" are load-bearing. One tool using a pattern heavily is one data point, not proof.
- **What clearing this bar looks like:** a survey across several real agent-facing dev tools (a code-search engine, a CLI proxy, a context-compression tool, a code-graph server) found `help[]`-shaped "note for the agent" hints independently reinvented, inconsistently, in every one of them.

Gate 1's ceiling ("stay generic" vs. "real tools need real sophistication") isn't a tension to compromise on — it's usually an architecture problem. Separate the _domain-specific decision_ from the _universal signal_.

# Dependency graphs (`michi-graph`)

`michi-graph` validates and orders dependency graphs: steps in a pipeline, operations in a release, packages in a workspace, tasks in an agent's plan. It is MIT-licensed, has no dependencies (it is `no_std` with `alloc`), and depends on nothing else in michi, so permissive crates such as `callisto-model` can use it. `michi-pipeline` builds its `Plan` on it.

It is a small, deterministic graph model, not a general graph library. There are no node or edge payloads, no mutation after a graph is built, no path finding and no execution policy. The reasons for each choice are in [06-decisions.md](06-decisions.md), "michi-graph: an MIT leaf crate, versioned on its own".

## Vocabulary

- A **node** has a key `K: Ord + Clone` chosen by the caller (`StepId`, `PackageId`, `String`).
- An **edge** says that a **dependent** depends on a **prerequisite**: the prerequisite comes first. The API never says "from/to" or "in/out", because those words mean opposite things in different tools.
- Every edge has a **kind** `E: Ord`, which defaults to `()`. Callisto uses kinds such as runtime, dev and peer; michi and wisp don't use kinds.
- A `NodeIx` is a node's declaration position: the first node declared is 0. It has no public constructor. Every method that takes one returns an empty slice or `None` for an index the graph does not have, so an index from another graph never panics.

## Building

```rust
let mut b = GraphBuilder::<StepId>::with_capacity(steps.len());
for step in &steps {
    let node = b.node(step.id().clone());
    for prerequisite in step.prerequisites() {
        b.depends_on(node, prerequisite, ());
    }
}
let graph = b.build(UnknownTargets::Error);
```

- `node(key)` declares a node and returns a `Decl` token. Edges hang off the token, not the key. A later node reusing a key is recorded as a duplicate, and its edges are dropped with it, so they can never land on the first node and cause false errors.
- `depends_on(decl, prerequisite, kind)` takes the prerequisite key, which may be declared before or after. An edge repeated with the same kind collapses into one.
- `build(policy)` never fails. It sets aside what it cannot use and records why, so every problem can be reported later in one list:
  - a duplicate node;
  - an edge to a key no node has (a **dangling** edge). It is always kept in `Graph::dangling()`. The `UnknownTargets` policy only decides whether validation reports it: `Error` reports it as `UnknownDependency`, and `Ignore` doesn't (Callisto ignores dependencies on packages outside the workspace);
  - more than `u32::MAX` nodes.
- A node that depends on itself is kept as an ordinary edge, and the edge filter decides whether it counts (a dev-only self-dependency is legal in Cargo).
- `Dag::from_nodes(iter, order)` builds and validates in one call for the common case: no kinds and unknown targets are errors.

## Graph and Dag

A `Graph<K, E>` may contain cycles. A `Dag<K>` is proven acyclic and carries no kinds, because validation has already chosen which edges count.

- `graph.validate(order)` uses every edge; `graph.validate_filtered(keep, order)` keeps only the edges for which `keep(EdgeRef)` returns true. `EdgeRef` has named fields: `dependent`, `prerequisite`, `kind` and both `NodeIx`s. Keys are shared between the graph and its dags, so validating does not copy them.
- One graph can produce several dags. Callisto validates its package graph once without dev edges for cascade order, and once with them for publish order.
- Validation returns the `Dag` or a `Violations` list with every problem at once. Cycles made only of filtered-out edges are not problems: you validate the graph you will run.
- When several kinds connect the same pair and more than one passes the filter, the dag holds one edge. `prerequisites` and `dependents` never repeat a node.
- `graph.cycles(keep, order)` reports the cycles of a graph that is allowed to have them (lumen's agent trajectories).

## Order

The caller chooses how ties are broken, once, at validation:

- `Order::Declaration`: the earliest-declared node first. Steps run in the order they were written. michi uses this.
- `Order::Key`: the smallest key first. Shuffling the declarations changes nothing. Callisto uses this, because it seals its release plan with a digest.

Everything the crate outputs follows that one order: the topological order, each layer, `ready`, `ancestors`, `descendants`, cycle members and the order of the violations' cycles. The topological order is the lexicographically smallest valid order under that rule, and that is part of the contract, not an implementation detail. The order never comes from hash maps or traversal accidents.

## Queries on a Dag

| Method | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `order()` | `&[NodeIx]` in topological order, computed at validation |
| `keys_in_order()` | the keys in that order |
| `prerequisites(ix)`, `dependents(ix)` | `&[NodeIx]` neighbours, in the chosen order |
| `layers()` | layer 0 has no prerequisites; a node's layer is one more than its deepest prerequisite's. Nodes in one layer don't depend on each other, so they can run together |
| `ready(satisfied, eligible)` | nodes for which `eligible(key)` holds and `satisfied(p)` holds for every prerequisite, in order |
| `ancestors(roots)`, `descendants(roots)` | every node upstream or downstream of `roots`, not including them |
| `key(ix)`, `index_of(&key)`, `node_at(position)`, `len()` | lookups; `node_at` maps a declaration position to its node, for callers that keep per-node data in declaration order |
| `canonical()` | each node's key with its prerequisites' keys, nodes and prerequisites sorted by key, for callers that hash the structure with their own hasher. Isolated nodes are included |

`ready` takes two predicates because callers track more than "done". A node behind a failure must not become ready, and a running or failed node is not eligible to start. When `satisfied` holds only for nodes that succeeded, checking direct prerequisites is enough: a node whose prerequisite failed can never become ready.

`ready` is one pass over the graph, O(V + E). There is no incremental ready tracker: michi's scheduler keeps its own counters because what unblocks a step depends on the outcome, and Callisto's release plans are small. A tracker can be added later without a breaking change if a consumer measures a need.

## Violations

`Violation<K>` is `#[non_exhaustive]` and holds keys, cloned only on the error path:

- `DuplicateNode { key }`
- `UnknownDependency { dependent, prerequisite }`
- `SelfDependency { key }`: reported once per node, never as a cycle.
- `Cycle(Cycle<K>)`: `members()` lists every node of one strongly connected component, in the chosen order. `path()` is one shortest closed path through the first member, so a message can show a real loop.
- `TooManyNodes`

`Violations<K>` lists them in a fixed order: duplicates, then edge problems by the dependent's declaration position and the edge's position, then cycles in the chosen order. The same input always gives the same list.

`Display` exists when `K: Display`, and `display_with(|key, f| ...)` covers keys without it. A cycle reads as `a depends on b, which depends on c, which depends on a`. The printed path stops after 8 steps with `… and N more`; the struct keeps the whole path. `Violations<K>` implements `core::error::Error` when `K: Debug + Display`.

## Implementation rules

- No recursion: Kahn's algorithm for the order and an iterative Kosaraju for strongly connected components. A 100,000-node chain and a 100,000-node cycle are tested.
- Kahn's leftovers are always an error: nodes on or behind a cycle never disappear silently. Strongly connected components are computed only on those leftovers, so a valid graph doesn't pay for them.
- Adjacency is `u32` indices in sorted vectors; keys live once in an `Arc<[K]>`, and a key-sorted index permutation answers `index_of` by binary search.
- No `unwrap`, `expect`, unchecked indexing or `unsafe` (`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`).

## How michi-pipeline uses it

- `Plan::new` declares one node per step, builds with `UnknownTargets::Error` and validates with `Order::Declaration`. Violations map one to one onto `PlanViolation`. Cycles stay a single `PlanViolation::Cycle` listing every step on any cycle in declaration order, and `TooManyNodes` becomes `PlanViolation::TooManySteps`. One change: a step stuck between two cycles (depending on one, depended on by another) lies on no cycle and is no longer listed.
- The scheduler reads `order()`, `prerequisites` and `dependents`. Node indices are declaration positions, so they match `Plan::steps()` and `RunRecord` without translation. Its ready counters, failure skipping and resume seeding stay in michi-pipeline: they are execution policy.
- `PlanFingerprint` stays michi's own 64-bit FNV-1a with its current framing, computed over `canonical()`. A record saved before the change still resumes.
- No michi-graph type appears in michi-pipeline's public API, so a michi-graph release never forces a breaking michi-pipeline release. michi-pipeline depends on it with a normal `^` range, not the exact pin the lockstep crates use.

## Licensing and release

- `license = "MIT"` in the crate's own manifest and a crate `LICENSE`; the rest of the workspace stays FSL-1.1-MIT.
- CI walks the normal and build dependencies of `michi-graph` with `cargo metadata` and fails on any license outside the permissive allowlist, so no FSL crate can enter its tree.
- It versions on its own, outside the Callisto fixed group `michi`. A michi-graph minor release moves michi-pipeline out of its `^` range, so Callisto's cascade also bumps the michi group.

/// Strongly connected components of the subgraph induced by `members` (Kosaraju, iterative). Only components that
/// form a cycle are returned: two or more nodes, or one node with an edge to itself (`self_loop`).
pub(crate) fn cyclic_components(
    members: &[bool],
    forward: &Csr,
    backward: &Csr,
    self_loop: &[bool],
) -> Vec<Vec<NodeIx>> {
    let n = members.len();
    let inside = |i: usize| members.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(false);

    // Pass 1: finish order of a depth-first search over `forward`.
    let mut visited = vec![false; n];
    let mut finished: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    let mut stack: Vec<(usize, usize)> = Vec::new();
    for root in 0..n {
        if !inside(root) || visited.get(root).copied().unwrap_or(true) {
            continue;
        }
        mark(&mut visited, root);
        stack.push((root, 0));
        while let Some(top) = stack.last_mut() {
            let (node, next) = *top;
            match forward.of(node).get(next) {
                Some(child) => {
                    top.1 += 1;
                    let c = child.u();
                    if inside(c) && !visited.get(c).copied().unwrap_or(true) {
                        mark(&mut visited, c);
                        stack.push((c, 0));
                    }
                }
                None => {
                    finished.push(node);
                    stack.pop();
                }
            }
        }
    }

    // Pass 2: in reverse finish order, everything reachable over `backward` is one component.
    let mut assigned = vec![false; n];
    let mut components = Vec::new();
    let mut frontier: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    for &root in finished.iter().rev() {
        if assigned.get(root).copied().unwrap_or(true) {
            continue;
        }
        mark(&mut assigned, root);
        let mut component = vec![NodeIx(root as u32)];
        frontier.push(root);
        while let Some(node) = frontier.pop() {
            for p in backward.of(node) {
                let i = p.u();
                if inside(i) && !assigned.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(true) {
                    mark(&mut assigned, i);
                    component.push(*p);
                    frontier.push(i);
                }
            }
        }
        let cyclic = component.len() > 1 || self_loop.get(root).copied().unwrap_or(false);
        if cyclic {
            components.push(component);
        }
    }
    components
}

fn mark(flags: &mut [bool], i: usize) {
    if let Some(f) = flags.get_mut(i) {
        *f = true;
    }
}

/// One shortest closed path through `start` that stays inside `component`, following `forward` edges. The path
/// lists `start` first and does not repeat it at the end.
pub(crate) fn shortest_cycle(start: NodeIx, component: &[bool], forward: &Csr) -> Vec<NodeIx> {
    let n = component.len();
    let mut parent: Vec<u32> = vec![u32::MAX; n];
    let mut queue = alloc::collections::VecDeque::new();
    queue.push_back(start.u());
    let mut seen = vec![false; n];
    mark(&mut seen, start.u());
    while let Some(node) = queue.pop_front() {
        for next in forward.of(node) {
            let i = next.u();
            if i == start.u() {
                let mut path = vec![NodeIx(node as u32)];
                let mut at = node;
                while at != start.u() {
                    let Some(&p) = parent.get(at) else { break };
                    if p == u32::MAX {
                        break;
                    }
                    path.push(NodeIx(p));
                    at = p as usize;
                }
                path.reverse();
                return path;
            }
            if component.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(false) && !seen.get(i).copied().unwrap_or(true) {
                mark(&mut seen, i);
                if let Some(slot) = parent.get_mut(i) {
                    *slot = node as u32;
                }
                queue.push_back(i);
            }
        }
    }
    vec![start]
}

//! A validated, acyclic graph and its queries.

use alloc::sync::Arc;
use alloc::vec;
use alloc::vec::Vec;
use core::borrow::Borrow;

use crate::algo::Csr;
use crate::builder::lookup;
use crate::graph::Kept;
use crate::violation::Violations;
use crate::{GraphBuilder, NodeIx, Order, UnknownTargets};

/// A graph proven to have no cycles, with the edges validation kept. Immutable; cheap to clone.
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Dag<K> {
    keys: Arc<[K]>,
    by_key: Arc<[u32]>,
    prerequisites: Arc<Csr>,
    dependents: Arc<Csr>,
    order: Arc<[NodeIx]>,
    rank: Arc<[u32]>,
    by_rank: Arc<[u32]>,
}

/// The layers of a [`Dag`]: layer 0 holds nodes without prerequisites, and a node's layer is one more than its deepest
/// prerequisite's. Nodes in one layer do not depend on each other.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Layers {
    nodes: Vec<NodeIx>,
    bounds: Vec<usize>,
}

impl Layers {
    /// Number of layers.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.bounds.len().saturating_sub(1)
    }

    /// Whether there are no layers (the dag is empty).
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len() == 0
    }

    /// Layer `i`, in the dag's [`Order`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn get(&self, i: usize) -> Option<&[NodeIx]> {
        let (&start, &end) = (self.bounds.get(i)?, self.bounds.get(i + 1)?);
        self.nodes.get(start..end)
    }

    /// Iterates the layers, first to last.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &[NodeIx]> + '_ {
        (0..self.len()).filter_map(|i| self.get(i))
    }
}

impl<K: Ord + Clone> Dag<K> {
    pub(crate) fn new(keys: Arc<[K]>, by_key: Arc<[u32]>, kept: Kept, order: Vec<NodeIx>) -> Self {
        Self {
            keys,
            by_key,
            prerequisites: Arc::new(kept.prerequisites),
            dependents: Arc::new(kept.dependents),
            order: Arc::from(order),
            rank: Arc::from(kept.rank),
            by_rank: Arc::from(kept.by_rank),
        }
    }

    /// Builds and validates in one call, for graphs without edge kinds where an unknown dependency is an error.
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// [`Violations`] listing every problem when the nodes do not form a valid dag.
    pub fn from_nodes<I, D>(nodes: I, order: Order) -> Result<Self, Violations<K>>
    where
        I: IntoIterator<Item = (K, D)>,
        D: IntoIterator<Item = K>,
    {
        let nodes = nodes.into_iter();
        let mut b = GraphBuilder::<K>::with_capacity(nodes.size_hint().0);
        for (key, prerequisites) in nodes {
            let node = b.node(key);
            for p in prerequisites {
                b.depends_on(node, p, ());
            }
        }
        b.build(UnknownTargets::Error).validate(order)
    }

    /// Number of nodes.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.keys.len()
    }

    /// Whether the dag has no nodes.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.keys.is_empty()
    }

    /// The key of node `ix`.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn key(&self, ix: NodeIx) -> Option<&K> {
        self.keys.get(ix.u())
    }

    /// The node at declaration position `position`, for callers that keep per-node data in declaration order. Valid
    /// only for a dag whose graph had no duplicate declarations, which validation guarantees.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn node_at(&self, position: usize) -> Option<NodeIx> {
        if position < self.len() {
            u32::try_from(position).ok().map(NodeIx)
        } else {
            None
        }
    }

    /// The node with `key`.
    pub fn index_of<Q>(&self, key: &Q) -> Option<NodeIx>
    where
        K: Borrow<Q>,
        Q: Ord + ?Sized,
    {
        lookup(&self.keys, &self.by_key, key).map(NodeIx)
    }

    /// The nodes in topological order: the lexicographically smallest valid order under the dag's [`Order`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn order(&self) -> &[NodeIx] {
        &self.order
    }

    /// The keys in topological order.
    pub fn keys_in_order(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &K> + '_ {
        self.order.iter().filter_map(|&ix| self.key(ix))
    }

    /// The nodes `ix` depends on, in the dag's [`Order`]. Empty for an index the dag does not have.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn prerequisites(&self, ix: NodeIx) -> &[NodeIx] {
        self.prerequisites.of(ix.u())
    }

    /// The nodes that depend on `ix`, in the dag's [`Order`]. Empty for an index the dag does not have.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn dependents(&self, ix: NodeIx) -> &[NodeIx] {
        self.dependents.of(ix.u())
    }

    /// The dag's layers. See [`Layers`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn layers(&self) -> Layers {
        let n = self.len();
        let mut depth = vec![0usize; n];
        for &ix in self.order.iter() {
            let d = self.prerequisites(ix).iter().filter_map(|p| depth.get(p.u())).max().map_or(0, |d| d + 1);
            if let Some(slot) = depth.get_mut(ix.u()) {
                *slot = d;
            }
        }
        let layers = depth.iter().max().map_or(0, |d| d + 1);
        let mut bounds = vec![0usize; layers + 1];
        for &d in &depth {
            if let Some(b) = bounds.get_mut(d + 1) {
                *b += 1;
            }
        }
        for i in 1..bounds.len() {
            let prev = bounds.get(i - 1).copied().unwrap_or(0);
            if let Some(b) = bounds.get_mut(i) {
                *b += prev;
            }
        }
        let mut cursor = bounds.clone();
        let mut nodes = vec![NodeIx(0); n];
        for &i in self.by_rank.iter() {
            let Some(&d) = depth.get(i as usize) else { continue };
            if let Some(c) = cursor.get_mut(d) {
                if let Some(slot) = nodes.get_mut(*c) {
                    *slot = NodeIx(i);
                }
                *c += 1;
            }
        }
        Layers { nodes, bounds }
    }

    /// The nodes that can start now: those for which `eligible(key)` holds and `satisfied(key)` holds for every
    /// prerequisite, in the dag's [`Order`]. One pass over the graph.
    ///
    /// When `satisfied` holds only for nodes that succeeded, a node behind a failure never becomes ready, so direct
    /// prerequisites are enough.
    pub fn ready<'a, S, R>(&'a self, satisfied: S, eligible: R) -> impl Iterator<Item = NodeIx> + 'a
    where
        S: Fn(&K) -> bool + 'a,
        R: Fn(&K) -> bool + 'a,
    {
        self.by_rank.iter().map(|&i| NodeIx(i)).filter(move |&ix| {
            self.key(ix).is_some_and(&eligible)
                && self.prerequisites(ix).iter().all(|&p| self.key(p).is_some_and(&satisfied))
        })
    }

    /// Every node upstream of `roots`, not including the roots, in the dag's [`Order`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn ancestors(&self, roots: &[NodeIx]) -> Vec<NodeIx> {
        self.closure(roots, &self.prerequisites)
    }

    /// Every node downstream of `roots`, not including the roots, in the dag's [`Order`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn descendants(&self, roots: &[NodeIx]) -> Vec<NodeIx> {
        self.closure(roots, &self.dependents)
    }

    fn closure(&self, roots: &[NodeIx], next: &Csr) -> Vec<NodeIx> {
        let n = self.len();
        let mut seen = vec![false; n];
        let mut stack: Vec<NodeIx> = Vec::new();
        for r in roots {
            if let Some(s) = seen.get_mut(r.u()) {
                *s = true;
                stack.push(*r);
            }
        }
        let mut found = Vec::new();
        while let Some(ix) = stack.pop() {
            for &m in next.of(ix.u()) {
                if let Some(s) = seen.get_mut(m.u()) {
                    if !*s {
                        *s = true;
                        found.push(m);
                        stack.push(m);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        found.sort_unstable_by_key(|ix| self.rank.get(ix.u()).copied().unwrap_or(u32::MAX));
        found
    }

    /// Each node's key with its prerequisites' keys, nodes and prerequisites sorted by key, isolated nodes included:
    /// a canonical form of the structure for callers that hash it with their own hasher.
    pub fn canonical(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&K, Vec<&K>)> + '_ {
        self.by_key.iter().filter_map(move |&i| {
            let key = self.keys.get(i as usize)?;
            let mut prerequisites: Vec<&K> =
                self.prerequisites.of(i as usize).iter().filter_map(|&p| self.key(p)).collect();
            prerequisites.sort_unstable();
            Some((key, prerequisites))
        })
    }
}

//! What validation reports.

use alloc::vec::Vec;
use core::fmt;

/// Steps of a cycle path printed before the rest is summarized.
const PATH_LIMIT: usize = 8;

/// One strongly connected component that forms a cycle.
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Cycle<K> {
    members: Vec<K>,
    path: Vec<K>,
}

impl<K> Cycle<K> {
    pub(crate) fn new(members: Vec<K>, path: Vec<K>) -> Self {
        Self { members, path }
    }

    /// Every node of the component, in the validation's [`crate::Order`].
    #[must_use]
    pub fn members(&self) -> &[K] {
        &self.members
    }

    /// One shortest loop through the first member: each node depends on the next, and the last depends on the first.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn path(&self) -> &[K] {
        &self.path
    }

    fn write(
        &self,
        f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>,
        key: &dyn Fn(&K, &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result,
    ) -> fmt::Result {
        let Some(first) = self.path.first() else { return f.write_str("dependency cycle") };
        f.write_str("dependency cycle: ")?;
        key(first, f)?;
        for (i, k) in self.path.iter().skip(1).enumerate() {
            if i == PATH_LIMIT {
                return write!(f, " … and {} more", self.path.len() - 1 - PATH_LIMIT);
            }
            f.write_str(if i == 0 { " depends on " } else { ", which depends on " })?;
            key(k, f)?;
        }
        f.write_str(if self.path.len() == 1 { " depends on " } else { ", which depends on " })?;
        key(first, f)
    }
}

/// One problem found by validation.
#[non_exhaustive]
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Violation<K> {
    /// A later declaration reuses an earlier node's key. Its edges were dropped.
    DuplicateNode {
        /// The repeated key.
        key: K,
    },
    /// A node depends on a key no node has.
    UnknownDependency {
        /// The node declaring the dependency.
        dependent: K,
        /// The missing key.
        prerequisite: K,
    },
    /// A node depends on itself. Reported once per node, never as a cycle.
    SelfDependency {
        /// The node.
        key: K,
    },
    /// Nodes that depend on each other in a loop.
    Cycle(Cycle<K>),
    /// More than `u32::MAX - 1` nodes were declared; the rest were dropped.
    TooManyNodes,
}

impl<K> Violation<K> {
    fn write(
        &self,
        f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>,
        key: &dyn Fn(&K, &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result,
    ) -> fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::DuplicateNode { key: k } => {
                f.write_str("duplicate node ")?;
                key(k, f)
            }
            Self::UnknownDependency { dependent, prerequisite } => {
                key(dependent, f)?;
                f.write_str(" depends on unknown node ")?;
                key(prerequisite, f)
            }
            Self::SelfDependency { key: k } => {
                key(k, f)?;
                f.write_str(" depends on itself")
            }
            Self::Cycle(cycle) => cycle.write(f, key),
            Self::TooManyNodes => write!(f, "more than {} nodes", u32::MAX - 1),
        }
    }
}

impl<K: fmt::Display> fmt::Display for Violation<K> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        self.write(f, &|k, f| k.fmt(f))
    }
}

impl<K: fmt::Display> fmt::Display for Cycle<K> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        self.write(f, &|k, f| k.fmt(f))
    }
}

/// Every problem validation found, in a fixed order: duplicates, then edge problems by the dependent's declaration
/// position and the edge's, then cycles in the validation's [`crate::Order`]. Never empty.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Violations<K> {
    list: Vec<Violation<K>>,
}

impl<K> Violations<K> {
    pub(crate) fn new(list: Vec<Violation<K>>) -> Self {
        Self { list }
    }

    /// The violations.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn as_slice(&self) -> &[Violation<K>] {
        &self.list
    }

    /// The violations, owned.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn into_vec(self) -> Vec<Violation<K>> {
        self.list
    }

    /// Iterates the violations.
    pub fn iter(&self) -> core::slice::Iter<'_, Violation<K>> {
        self.list.iter()
    }

    /// Renders with `key` writing each key, for key types without `Display`.
    pub fn display_with<F>(&self, key: F) -> impl fmt::Display + '_
    where
        F: Fn(&K, &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result + 'static,
    {
        DisplayWith { violations: self, key }
    }

    fn write(
        &self,
        f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>,
        key: &dyn Fn(&K, &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result,
    ) -> fmt::Result {
        for (i, v) in self.list.iter().enumerate() {
            if i > 0 {
                f.write_str("; ")?;
            }
            v.write(f, key)?;
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

impl<'a, K> IntoIterator for &'a Violations<K> {
    type Item = &'a Violation<K>;
    type IntoIter = core::slice::Iter<'a, Violation<K>>;
    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.list.iter()
    }
}

impl<K> IntoIterator for Violations<K> {
    type Item = Violation<K>;
    type IntoIter = alloc::vec::IntoIter<Violation<K>>;
    fn into_iter(self) -> Self::IntoIter {
        self.list.into_iter()
    }
}

impl<K: fmt::Display> fmt::Display for Violations<K> {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        self.write(f, &|k, f| k.fmt(f))
    }
}

impl<K: fmt::Debug + fmt::Display> core::error::Error for Violations<K> {}

struct DisplayWith<'a, K, F> {
    violations: &'a Violations<K>,
    key: F,
}

impl<K, F> fmt::Display for DisplayWith<'_, K, F>
where
    F: Fn(&K, &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result,
{
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        self.violations.write(f, &self.key)
    }
}
